### Symbols for learning

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $n$ | sample size: number of observations |
| $d$ | number of features, the input dimension |
| $\mathcal X$, $\mathcal Y$ | input (domain) space, label space |
| $\mathcal D$ | data distribution on $\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y$ |
| $S = ((\mathbf x_i, y_i))_{i=1}^n$ | training sample |
| $\mathbf x_i$, $y_i$ | feature vector and label of the $i$-th observation |
| $\mathbf X$ | data (design) matrix, with rows $\mathbf x_i^\top$ |
| $\mathbf y$ | vector of the $n$ labels |
| $\hat y$ | prediction of a label |
| $h$ | hypothesis (predictor) |
| $\ell(\hat y, y)$, $\ell(h, z)$ | loss of a prediction, loss of $h$ on an example $z$ |
| $L_{\mathcal D}(h)$ | true risk, $\mathbb E_{z\sim\mathcal D}[\ell(h, z)]$ |
| $L_S(h)$ | empirical risk (training loss) on $S$ |
| $\boldsymbol\theta$ | model parameters |
| $\mathbf w$, $w_0$ | weights and intercept of a linear model |
| $\eta$ | learning rate (step size of gradient descent) |
| $t$ | iteration or time index |
| $\delta$ | confidence (failure probability) of a PAC or concentration bound, whose accuracy is a small $\varepsilon$ |
| $m_{\mathcal H}(\varepsilon, \delta)$ | sample complexity of a hypothesis class |
| $\operatorname{VCdim}$ | VC dimension |
| $\hat{\mathfrak R}_S$ | empirical Rademacher complexity on $S$ |
| $\boldsymbol\phi(\mathbf x)$ | feature map |
| $k(\mathbf x, \mathbf x')$, $\mathbf K$ | kernel, Gram matrix $K_{ij} = k(\mathbf x_i, \mathbf x_j)$ |
| $K$ | number of classes or clusters |
| $l$ | layer index of a network |
| $\mathbf W^{(l)}$, $\mathbf b^{(l)}$, $\mathbf h^{(l)}$ | weights, biases and activations of layer $l$ |
| $\mathrm{Regret}_T$ | regret after $T$ rounds |
| $(\mathcal S, \mathcal A, P, R, \gamma)$ | Markov decision process: state space, action space, transition kernel, reward, discount |
| $S_t$, $A_t$, $R_{t+1}$ | state, action and reward random variables; the reward of step $t$ is $R_{t+1}$ |
| $s$, $a$, $s'$ | values of states and actions |
| $P(s' \mid s, a)$ | transition kernel |
| $\mathbf P_\pi$ | transition matrix under the policy $\pi$ |
| $\gamma$ | discount factor |
| $\pi(a \mid s)$ | policy |
| $\pi_{\boldsymbol\theta}(s)$ | deterministic policy |
| $b(a \mid s)$ | behaviour policy |
| $\mu_\pi$ | on-policy state distribution |
| $G_t$ | discounted return |
| $v_\pi$, $q_\pi$ | state-value and action-value functions |
| $v_*$, $q_*$ | optimal value functions |
| $V$, $Q$ | tabular estimates of $v_\pi$, $q_\pi$ |
| $\hat v(s, \mathbf w)$, $\hat q(s, a, \mathbf w)$ | approximate value functions |
| $a_\pi(s, a)$ | advantage, $q_\pi(s, a) - v_\pi(s)$ |
| $\hat A_t$ | advantage estimate |
| $\delta_t$ | temporal-difference error |
| $\rho_t(\boldsymbol\theta)$ | probability ratio of PPO and of importance sampling |
| $\tau$ | trajectory |
| $J(\boldsymbol\theta)$ | objective to maximise |
| $\mathcal B$ | replay buffer |

Conventions:

- Vectors and matrices are bold; the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ is the one plain exception.
- The sample size is $n$, the input dimension $d$.
- The loss is $\ell$, the risk $L$; a likelihood is written $p(S \mid \boldsymbol\theta)$ and a log-likelihood
  $\log p(S \mid \boldsymbol\theta)$, with no separate letter.
- Reinforcement learning follows Sutton and Barto: uppercase random variables $S_t$, $A_t$, $R_{t+1}$, true values
  $v_\pi$, $q_\pi$, estimates $V$, $Q$, $\hat v$, $\hat q$.
